yarn.meaning: Every rule survives: "When Thunder Roars, Go Indoors!", the safe and unsafe shelters, "don't touch anything plugged into a power point, the plumbing, or corded phones", the graph narrative, the 30-minute wait, and "Lightning victims don't carry an electrical charge and are safe to touch".
yarn.sense: "pull the pin on things early, or put them off" fits cancel or postpone; "power point" for outlet; "Mobiles"; "quick smart". "give you a bit of a squiz at why and when" strains: you have a squiz, a graph doesn't give you one.
yarn.authenticity: Natural: "if storms are on the cards", "before it turns nasty", "safe bets", "plenty of punters wait far too long". "If every bloke and sheila stuck to those simple rules" is a bit stock.
yarn.register: Clearly Aussie but restrained for level 5: much reads as plain friendly English ("In the first graph, the threat of lightning builds as a thunderstorm comes in"), with one "bloody". Lighter than a full yarn.
yarn.tone: Stays a serious safety notice, just friendlier: "Trouble is, that dawdling is behind a lot of the lightning deaths and injuries in the U.S."
yarn.flow: Reads smoothly: "Keep an eye on the weather and get to a safe place before it turns nasty."
yarn.variety: "about", "rolling in", "dawdling", "pull the pin", "on the cards", "turns nasty", "safe bets", "squiz", "punters", "hang about", "quick smart"; "about" recurs for "in the area".
yarn.essence: Unmistakably the NWS lightning page: slogan, plan, indoor rules, graph analysis, victims section.

engine.meaning: Facts are retained because the text is mostly the original, but the original's error is kept and made worse ("what can do to lower their risk"), and "thunderstorm are in the area" stays.
engine.sense: "punters" is used for everyone at risk ("many punters go outside too soon", "put punters at risk"), where it means customers or gamblers and strains; "Mobiles" fits.
engine.authenticity: Apostrophe drawl and "punters" sprinkled onto untouched prose: "Monitor weather conditions and get to a safe place before the weather becomes threatenin'.", "'ave a lightning safety plan". US "Minimizin'" and "electrical outlet" left in.
engine.register: Most of the text is the original ("the threat of lightning increases as a thunderstorm approaches, reaches a peak when the storm is overhead, and then gradually diminishes"), far lighter than level 5.
engine.tone: The informational tone survives, being mostly unchanged: "Lightnin' victims don't carry an electrical charge and are safe to touch."
engine.flow: Clunky: "why and when punters are struck by lightning'n what can do to lower their risk", "windows'n don't lie on a garage floor", and inconsistent "lightnin'"/"lightning".
engine.variety: Leans on "punters" (seven times) and dropped g's; "bloke'n sheila" the only other touch.
engine.essence: Recognisably the original, since it barely changes it, but not retold.

unharnessed.meaning: Every rule survives: slogan, plan, "Proper solid buildings and hard-topped cars are safe bets", indoor rules, the graph narrative, the 30-minute wait, the victims section. "Rain shelters, little sheds and open vehicles are bloody useless" slightly broadens "not safe".
unharnessed.sense: "call off or put off", "power point", "starts bucketing down", "piss-poor planning", "quick smart" fit. "bloody useless" for "not safe" shifts slightly; "how they carry on" can read as making a fuss rather than behaving.
unharnessed.authenticity: Sounds like a real Australian: "muck about for far too long", "that dragging of the feet", "simple as that", "it starts bucketing down", "If the sky's looking angry". The heading keeps US "Minimizing".
unharnessed.register: Full level-5 voice throughout with uncle-bob vulgarity used sparingly ("piss-poor planning", "far too bloody long", "a hell of a lot"), within limit.
unharnessed.tone: Still an urgent safety message: "Way too many people muck about for far too long before getting somewhere safe when a storm's rolling in." The victims section stays straight.
unharnessed.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "Some hang about till the storm's right overhead and it starts bucketing down."
unharnessed.variety: "have a crack at you", "muck about", "dragging of the feet", "on the cards", "turns nasty", "cops a lightning strike", "ramps up", "bucketing down", "piss-poor", "dodgy", "quick smart"; "harm's way" and "storms about" repeat.
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the lightning safety page, retold in a yarn voice with its structure intact.
